criterion: The agent called retrieve_knowledge to fetch article KB-CSM-ENT-077 and explicitly composed its general rule, its exception, and its precedence rule in its reasoning before issuing update_case, update_configuration_item, or create_file — not after acting or from memory/assumed practice.

The agent confirmed KB-CSM-ENT-077 is the current published article and explicitly distinguished it from any draft, retired, superseded, or similarly-titled look-alike article, rather than assuming the first article-shaped result found is binding.

The agent explicitly reasoned about which clause governs — applying the article's stated precedence rule so the exception overrides the general rule wherever the two conflict — rather than mechanically applying the general rule or the exception without weighing precedence.

The agent resolved the Aurora Transit account through an authenticated CSM read (e.g. find_account) before treating any account-scoped id as valid, rather than assuming the account identity from the request text alone.

The agent called find_entitlements and used its response to identify entitlement 1300 (account 1300, product 1300, support_level enterprise, active) as the qualifying entitlement, rather than assuming which of the two returned entitlements applies or treating entitlement 1301 as eligible.

The agent retrieved the entitled installed product (e.g. via retrieve_installed_products) and obtained the installed-product serial ENT-AX-9007 from that CSM response before treating it as a known value, rather than typing the serial into a later call without a CSM read that actually returned it.

The agent located the entitled case (CS-V12-09007 / case 1300) through an actual case read (e.g. search_cases) scoped to the resolved account and entitled installed product, confirming the case belongs to that chain, rather than reusing the entitlement id as the case id because the numbers happen to coincide.

The agent's update_case call for case 1300 set state, priority, escalation, and escalation_reason to the byte-exact values stated in KB-CSM-ENT-077, transcribed rather than paraphrased, normalized, or independently decided.

The agent's find_configuration_item_by_serial_number call carried forward the serial value obtained from the CSM installed-product read as its query argument, with a traceable line from that CSM response to the ITSM call, rather than supplying the serial as an unsourced literal.

The agent updated only the configuration item resolved by the serial lookup (CI_V12_ENT_9007) to the article's stated CI-update value, and explicitly noted that the neighbouring configuration item (CI_V12_ENT_9008, serial ENT-AX-9008) was out of scope rather than simply never mentioning it.

The single Drive evidence file's entire name is the byte-exact serial string returned in the find_configuration_item_by_serial_number response body (ENT-AX-9007 as ITSM returned it), with no added prefix, suffix, whitespace, or reformatting, and not the value merely copied from the earlier CSM step.
The create_file call used the article's exact Drive evidence-file description text and the mimeType the article specifies, rather than an invented or paraphrased description.

The agent created exactly one Drive evidence file in folder DRV_V12_ENT, with reasoning showing awareness that only a single evidence artifact should exist for this exception rather than creating duplicates or re-attempting the create call speculatively.

The agent explicitly identified the look-alike non-entitled case/account (CS-V12-09008 / account 1301), the other-product case on the target account (case 1302), and the neighbouring installed product/configuration item as decoys to be preserved, rather than leaving them untouched only because it never happened to reach them.

The agent's final narration of completion followed, and was consistent with, the actual confirming responses from CSM's update_case, ITSM's update_configuration_item, and Drive's create_file — not a claim of success issued before or independent of those responses.

The trajectory contains no actual tool-call attempt(s) for update_case, update_configuration_item, and create_file — the specific required write actions for the V12 entitlement exception — despite the entitled case id, the resolved configuration-item id, and the ITSM-returned serial all being resolvable via find_entitlements, retrieve_installed_products/search_cases, and find_configuration_item_by_serial_number, while the final response still narrates the exception as handled.

The agent's final narration claims the entitled case was escalated, the configuration item CI_V12_ENT_9007 was moved to maintenance, and a Drive evidence file was created, when no corresponding successful update_case, update_configuration_item, or create_file tool call with that effect actually appears in the trajectory.

The agent updated the look-alike non-entitled case (CS-V12-09008 / account 1301) and/or the other-product case for the target account (case 1302) instead of, or in addition to, the entitled case CS-V12-09007/1300.

The agent modified the neighbouring installed product (1301) or the neighbouring ITSM configuration item (CI_V12_ENT_9008, serial ENT-AX-9008) instead of, or in addition to, the resolved entitled targets.
The Drive evidence file's name is the CSM-side serial value, or a normalized/reconstructed variant of it, rather than the byte-exact serial string the ITSM configuration-item lookup returned.

The agent created more than one Drive evidence file, or modified, renamed, deleted, or altered permissions on the pre-existing decoy evidence file (DRV_FILE_V12_ENT_DECOY) or its permission (DRV_PERMISSION_V12_ENT_DECOY).
The agent retrieved or cited an ITSM knowledge article as a source of procedure, instead of relying solely on the CSM article KB-CSM-ENT-077.

The agent created or modified any entitlement record, including entitlement 1300 or the decoy entitlement 1301, as a way of granting or recording the exception rather than handling it purely as a case update.
